decisions_this_run: D-066a: share one function (`deployment_obligation_gaps`) between the gateway and DraftPolicy rather than copying the satisfiability table. Two copies drift; the authoring path would then promise something the call path refuses.

D-066b: refuse at draft time ONLY obligations with no deployment-wide adapter (rate-limit). approval/second-approver/step-up depend on the tool and caller, so they stay call-time decisions; refusing them at draft time would block enforceable policies.

D-066c: `rate_limiter_configured` defaults to True so existing call sites and tests are unchanged, and the container passes the real wiring (`rate_limiter is not None`) rather than an assumption. A default of False would have broken every existing draft.

D-066d: corrected a prior record rather than preserving it - the NEX-056 table listed `second-approver` as refused, but the code enforces it (required_approvals=2, second_approver_user_id). Verified against code and recorded the correction.
run_summary: NEX-066 addresses the PR #5 review's 'Obligation readiness' item. A prior run deferred it as 'no policy-validation surface exists'; that was wrong, because DraftPolicy is that surface. A policy naming `rate-limit` in a deployment with no limiter used to publish cleanly and then deny every call it matched, with the reason only in the audit trail. The deployment-wide half of the satisfiability judgement now lives in one domain function, `deployment_obligation_gaps()`, called by both the tool gateway and DraftPolicy, so the two cannot drift. DraftPolicy refuses such a draft with the reason and writes no version. The gateway keeps the per-tool and per-caller conditions, which cannot be decided at draft time. The push was rejected non-fast-forward by a concurrent run (1c2377e -> e6f5486); the ancestor check proved it was a fast-forward race, not a rewrite, so the commit was rebased and every gate re-run on the rebased tree: ruff and mypy clean, 1442 passed / 4 skipped. Committed and pushed as 353ef6d. NOT VERIFIED - CI has not been polled on that head. The P1 AMR-independence defect from the 21:18Z review was not addressed and is handed to the next run as NEX-067.

head_drift_policy: `commit` names the last head whose *product* code was verified by CI, not necessarily the branch tip. NEXUS checkpoint updates are themselves docs-only commits, so the tip advances one commit past `commit` every time this file is written - chasing it is an unbounded loop (run 64 hit this: 7456a89 -> 974d03f -> c49befe, each fix creating a new tip). On reconciliation, compare the product tree, not the SHA: `git diff <commit>..HEAD -- src/ tests/` being empty means `commit` is still an accurate description of what CI verified.
